messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- The section never calls sdk.call, except "Vera.Ask.text" as said below: what the phone does is not its job.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them.
- If the section cannot really do it with this language and these components -- it needs a camera, a live feed, the person's location or data the phone does not hold -- decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it with made-up data.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

<classes>
</classes>
<fields>
</fields>
<functions>
function c_parseDay(state: AppState): number {
  let s: string = strings.trim(state.birthDate);
  if (strings.length(s) === 0) { return -1; }
  let parts: string[] = strings.split(s, "-");
  if (parts.length() !== 3) { return -1; }
  let y: number = strings.toNumber(parts[0], -1);
  let m: number = strings.toNumber(parts[1], -1);
  let d: number = strings.toNumber(parts[2], -1);
  if (y < 1900 || y > 2200) { return -1; }
  if (m < 1 || m > 12) { return -1; }
  if (d < 1 || d > 31) { return -1; }
  let a: number = math.floor((14 - m) / 12);
  let yy: number = y + 4800 - a;
  let mm: number = m + 12 * a - 3;
  let jdn: number = d + math.floor((153 * mm + 2) / 5) + 365 * yy + math.floor(yy / 4) - math.floor(yy / 100) + math.floor(yy / 400) - 32045;
  let epoch: number = 2440588;
  return jdn - epoch;
}

function c_ageDays(state: AppState): number {
  let day: number = c_parseDay(state);
  if (day < 0) { return -1; }
  let today: number = time.daysSinceEpoch();
  let diff: number = today - day;
  if (diff < 0) { return -1; }
  return diff;
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let c_day: number = c_parseDay(state);
  let c_age: number = c_ageDays(state);
  let c_rows: ui.View[] = [];
  if (strings.length(strings.trim(state.birthDate)) === 0) {
    c_rows.push(ui.Text("caption", "Type your birth date as YYYY-MM-DD, for example 1990-05-14."));
  } else {
    if (c_day < 0) {
      c_rows.push(ui.InsetBanner("warning", "Check the date", "Use the form YYYY-MM-DD, for example 1990-05-14.", "", "", "warning"));
    } else {
      if (c_age < 0) {
        c_rows.push(ui.InsetBanner("warning", "Date is in the future", "The birth date must be today or earlier.", "", "", "warning"));
      } else {
        c_rows.push(ui.MetricGroup("default", 1, [
          ui.NumberStat("accent", "Age in days", c_age, "", " days", 1, "since " + state.birthDate, "calendar")
        ]));
      }
    }
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("summary", "Age in days", "", c_rows));
}
</view>

metadata.label: count-02
needs: the figure "Age in days": How many days have passed since the birth date (the plan works it out as floor((elapsed) / 86400); for elapsed = 31536000 that is 365)

metadata.label: flash-02
needs: A starter deck of vocabulary flashcards, each with a word on the front and its definition on the back, such as 'abundant — existing in large quantities', 'candid — honest and direct', 'diligent — showing careful effort', 'frugal — sparing with money', 'gregarious — fond of company', 'lucid — clear and easy to understand', 'meticulous — extremely careful about detail', 'resilient — able to recover quickly', 'tenacious — holding on firmly', 'vivid — producing strong clear images'. The person taps a card to flip it between word and definition, marks each card as known or missed, and the phone keeps the missed ones in a review pile.
Mark card known or missed
Review pile of missed words

<functions>
function c_play(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let seed: number = time.nowMillis() + state.c_shake * 7 + state.playerChoiceIndex * 13;
  let pick: number = math.randomBelow(seed, 3);
  let player: number = state.playerChoiceIndex;
  let result: string = "Draw";
  let wins: number = state.c_wins;
  let losses: number = state.c_losses;
  let draws: number = state.c_draws;
  if (player === pick) {
    result = "Draw";
    draws = draws + 1;
  } else {
    if ((player === 0 && pick === 2) || (player === 1 && pick === 0) || (player === 2 && pick === 1)) {
      result = "You win";
      wins = wins + 1;
    } else {
      result = "You lose";
      losses = losses + 1;
    }
  }
  return {c_computerChoice: pick, c_wins: wins, c_losses: losses, c_draws: draws, c_result: result, c_shake: state.c_shake + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_handPath(choice: number): string {
  if (choice === 0) {
    return "M50 20 C30 20 22 34 24 48 C26 62 38 70 50 70 C62 70 74 62 76 48 C78 34 70 20 50 20 Z";
  }
  if (choice === 1) {
    return "M20 30 L80 30 L80 70 L20 70 Z";
  }
  return "M30 20 L70 20 L70 80 L30 80 Z";
}

function c_handLabel(choice: number): string {
  if (choice === 0) { return "Rock"; }
  if (choice === 1) { return "Paper"; }
  return "Scissors";
}
</functions>

let c_playerShapes: ui.View[] = [];
c_playerShapes.push(ui.Path("accent", c_handPath(state.playerChoiceIndex), 0));
c_playerShapes.push(ui.Text("caption", c_handLabel(state.playerChoiceIndex)));
let c_computerShapes: ui.View[] = [];
c_computerShapes.push(ui.Path("warning", c_handPath(state.c_computerChoice), 0));
c_computerShapes.push(ui.Text("caption", c_handLabel(state.c_computerChoice)));
let c_hands: ui.View[] = [];
c_hands.push(ui.Column("center", c_playerShapes));
c_hands.push(ui.Text("title", "vs"));
c_hands.push(ui.Motion("shake", state.c_shake, [ui.Column("center", c_computerShapes)]));
let c_resultText: string = "Tap Play to throw";
if (state.c_result !== "") {
  c_resultText = state.c_result;
}
sections.push(ui.Section("hero", "", "", [
  ui.Card("surface", [
    ui.Row("center", c_hands),
    ui.Text("heading", c_resultText),
    ui.ActionBar("center", [
      ui.Button("primary", "Play", "c_play", 0, true)
    ])
  ]),
  ui.MetricGroup("default", 3, [
    ui.NumberStat("success", "Wins", state.c_wins, "", "", 1, "", "check"),
    ui.NumberStat("danger", "Losses", state.c_losses, "", "", 1, "", "close"),
    ui.NumberStat("default", "Draws", state.c_draws, "", "", 1, "", "minus")
  ])
]));

needs: Two hands face each other; on a tap the computer's hand shakes and lands on a random throw of rock, paper or scissors, the player's hand shows the chosen throw, and the scene decides win, lose or draw and keeps the running tally of wins, losses and draws.

}

  }
  return total;
}

function c_goal(state: AppState): number {
  return strings.toNumber(state.dailyGoalText, 0);
}

function c_toGo(state: AppState): number {
  let g: number = c_goal(state);
  let t: number = c_todaySteps(state);
  if (g - t < 0) { return 0; }
  return g - t;
}

  let g: number = c_goal(state);

}

function c_parseDate(s: string): number {
  let t: string = strings.trim(s);
  if (strings.length(t) !== 8) { return -1; }
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < 8) {
    let ch: string = strings.substring(t, i, i + 1);
    if (ch < "0" || ch > "9") { return -1; }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let y: number = strings.toNumber(strings.substring(t, 0, 4), -1);
  let m: number = strings.toNumber(strings.substring(t, 4, 6), -1);
  let d: number = strings.toNumber(strings.substring(t, 6, 8), -1);
  if (y < 1 || m < 1 || m > 12 || d < 1) { return -1; }
  let dim: number = 31;
  if (m === 4 || m === 6 || m === 9 || m === 11) { dim = 30; }
  if (m === 2) {
    dim = 28;
    if (y % 4 === 0) { dim = 29; }
    if (y % 100 === 0 && y % 400 !== 0) { dim = 28; }
  }
  if (d > dim) { return -1; }
  return y * 10000 + m * 100 + d;
}

function c_dayNumber(v: number): number {
  let y: number = math.floor(v / 10000);
  let m: number = math.floor(v / 100) % 100;
  let d: number = v % 100;
  let yy: number = y;
  if (m <= 2) { yy = yy - 1; }
  let era: number = math.floor(yy / 400);
  let yoe: number = yy - era * 400;
  let mp: number = m + 9;
  if (m > 2) { mp = m - 3; }
  let doy: number = math.floor((153 * mp + 2) / 5) + d - 1;
  let doe: number = yoe * 365 + math.floor(yoe / 4) - math.floor(yoe / 100) + doy;
  return era * 146097 + doe - 719468;
}

function c_totalDays(state: AppState): number {
  let a: number = c_parseDate(state.startDate);
  let b: number = c_parseDate(state.endDate);
  if (a < 0 || b < 0) { return -1; }
  let diff: number = c_dayNumber(b) - c_dayNumber(a);
  if (diff < 0) { return -1; }
  return diff;
}

function c_fullWeeks(state: AppState): number {
  let t: number = c_totalDays(state);
  if (t < 0) { return 0; }
  return math.floor(t / 7);
}

function c_weekdays(state: AppState): number {
  return c_fullWeeks(state) * 5;
}

function c_extraDays(state: AppState): number {
  let t: number = c_totalDays(state);
  if (t < 0) { return 0; }
  return t % 7;
}

function c_workingDays(state: AppState): number {
  let t: number = c_totalDays(state);
  if (t < 0) { return 0; }
  let extra: number = t % 7;
  let add: number = extra;
  if (add > 5) { add = 5; }
  return c_weekdays(state) + add;
}

function c_waysFor(state: AppState, target: number): number {
  let dice: number = state.diceCount;
  if (dice !== 2) { return 0; }
  let ways: number = 0;
  let a: number = 1;
  while (a <= 6) {
    let b: number = 1;
    while (b <= 6) {
      if (a + b === target) { ways = ways + 1; }
      b = b + 1;
    }
    a = a + 1;
  }
  return ways;
}

function c_total(state: AppState): number {
  return math.pow(6, state.diceCount);
}

function c_percent(state: AppState, target: number): number {
  let total: number = c_total(state);
  if (total === 0) { return 0; }
  return c_waysFor(state, target) / total * 100;
}

function c_log(x: number): number {
  if (x <= 0) { return 0; }
  let y: number = (x - 1) / (x + 1);
  let y2: number = y * y;
  let term: number = y;
  let sum: number = 0;
  let n: number = 0;
  while (n < 60) {
    sum = sum + term / (2 * n + 1);
    term = term * y2;
    n = n + 1;
  }
  return 2 * sum;
}

function c_months(balance: number, monthlyRate: number, monthlyPayment: number): number {
  if (balance <= 0) { return 0; }
  if (monthlyPayment <= 0) { return 0; }
  if (monthlyRate <= 0) {
    return math.ceil(balance / monthlyPayment);
  }
  let ratio: number = balance * monthlyRate / monthlyPayment;
  if (ratio >= 1) { return 0; }
  let months: number = -c_log(1 - ratio) / c_log(1 + monthlyRate);
  return math.ceil(months);
}
</functions>

  let w: string[] = ["because", "friend", "beautiful", "receive", "separate", "necessary", "definitely", "rhythm", "surprise", "tomorrow"];
  return w;
}

function c_wordAt(i: number): string {
  let w: string[] = c_words();
  if (i < 0 || i >= w.length()) { return ""; }
  return w[i];
}

function c_done(state: AppState): number {
  let n: number = state.c_answers.length();
  if (n > state.wordCount) { return state.wordCount; }
  return n;
}

function c_left(state: AppState): number {
  let left: number = state.wordCount - c_done(state);
  if (left < 0) { return 0; }
  return left;
}

function c_correct(state: AppState): number {
  let total: number = 0;
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.c_answers.length()) {
    if (state.c_answers[i] === c_wordAt(i)) { total = total + 1; }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return total;
}

  return {c_typed: value, c_showError: false__PASSTHROUGH__};

<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>

</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>

</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};

<functions>
function c_gapMinutes(state: AppState): number {
  let values: number[] = [15, 30, 45, 60];
  let i: number = state.reminderGapIndex;
  if (i < 0) { i = 0; }
  if (i > 3) { i = 3; }
  return values[i];
}

function c_windowMinutes(state: AppState): number {
  let span: number = state.endTime - state.startTime;
  if (span < 0) { span = span + 1440; }
  return span;
}

function c_remindersPerWindow(state: AppState): number {
  let gap: number = c_gapMinutes(state);
  if (gap <= 0) { return 0; }
  return math.floor(c_windowMinutes(state) / gap);
}

function c_buzz(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  sdk.call("SensorServiceKit.vibrator.vibrate", ["duration", "800"], "c_onBuzzAnswer");
  return {c_buzzPending: true, c_buzzMessage: "Buzzing..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_onBuzzAnswer(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  let failed: boolean = strings.startsWith(value, "declined") || strings.startsWith(value, "error");
  if (failed) {
    return {c_buzzPending: false, c_buzzMessage: "The buzz did not go through: " + value__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let minute: number = time.hourOfDay() * 60 + time.minuteOfHour();
  return {c_buzzPending: false, c_buzzMessage: "Buzzed at " + ui.clockToString(minute) + ". Straighten up.", c_buzzCount: state.c_buzzCount + 1, c_lastBuzz: ui.clockToString(minute)__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{

  let c_span: number = c_windowMinutes(state);
  let c_perWindow: number = c_remindersPerWindow(state);
  let c_rows: ui.View[] = [];
  c_rows.push(ui.KeyValueGroup("default", 2, [
    ui.KeyValueItem("default", "Buzz every", ui.numberToString(c_gap) + " min", ""),
    ui.KeyValueItem("default", "Window", ui.clockToString(state.startTime) + " - " + ui.clockToString(state.endTime), ui.durationToString(c_span * 60)),
    ui.KeyValueItem("default", "Reminders per window", ui.numberToString(c_perWindow), ""),
    ui.KeyValueItem("default", "Buzzed so far", ui.numberToString(state.c_buzzCount), state.c_lastBuzz)
  ]));

    ui.Button("primary", "Buzz now", "c_buzz", 0, !state.c_buzzPending)
  ]));

}
